title: Toric code / Z2 topological order
intro: H = -Je sum_s A_s - Jm sum_p B_p on an L x L torus.

questions.question: Ground-state energy of the L = 3 toric code (Je = Jm = 1)?
questions.explanation: -(Je + Jm) L^2 = -18; every stabiliser is satisfied.

questions.question: Ground-state degeneracy on the torus?
questions.explanation: 4 = |anyon types|: Wilson loops along both cycles take values +-1.

questions.question: Ground-state degeneracy on a genus-2 surface?
Energy of the lowest excitation (Je = Jm = 1)?
questions.explanation: Anyons come in pairs; each violated stabiliser costs 2, so the lowest e-pair costs 4.

questions.question: Topological entanglement entropy gamma (in nats)?
questions.explanation: gamma = ln D with total quantum dimension D = 2 for Z2: ln 2.

questions.question: Why does the Kitaev-Preskill combination S_A+S_B+S_C-S_AB-S_BC-S_CA+S_ABC isolate -gamma?
options: Boundary (area-law) and corner contributions cancel by inclusion-exclusion
questions.explanation: Every boundary segment appears with alternating signs; only the topological constant survives.

questions.question: Which is the e-particle (charge) of the toric code?
questions.explanation: Charges are star violations created by Z strings; fluxes (m) are plaquette violations created by X strings on the dual lattice. e x m = fermion.

questions.question: A large uniform field h_z eventually
questions.explanation: The field gives anyons kinetic energy; they condense near h ~ 0.33 (3D-Ising* transition). Try it with ED on L = 3 by watching the splitting of the 4 states.
